extracted.intended_audience: postdoctoral researchers applying for NIEHS NRSA Individual Postdoctoral (F32) fellowships and their sponsors/mentors
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and requirements for applying to the NIEHS Individual Postdoctoral Fellowship (NRSA F32), including eligibility, sponsor/institution expectations, allowable support, and program purpose. Intended to inform applicants and mentors preparing an F32 application to NIEHS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program purpose and candidate profile
rubrics_metrics.description: NRSA F32 fellowships provide up to three years of support for promising postdoctoral researchers who have the potential to become productive, independent investigators within the broad scope of biomedical, behavioral, or clinical research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellowships support training opportunities in environmental health sciences; the award aims to develop independence and research productivity in the fellow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Degree requirement before award activation
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the postdoctoral fellowship award can be activated, the individual must have received a Ph.D. or equivalent research degree, or a professional degree such as M.D., D.V.M., etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The doctoral or equivalent degree must be awarded prior to activation of the fellowship (i.e., applicants who have not yet received the degree at activation are not eligible).

rubrics_metrics.name: Citizenship / residency eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: At the time of the award, candidates for the postdoctoral fellowship must be U.S. citizens, noncitizen nationals, or permanent residents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should confirm their citizenship or permanent resident status at award time; other visa statuses are not listed as eligible here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsoring institution and sponsor identification
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting the fellowship application, the applicant must identify a sponsoring institution and an individual who will serve as a sponsor (mentor or supervisor) and who will supervise the training and research experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and secure agreement from the sponsor and host institution before application; the applicant should work with the sponsor in preparing the application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sponsor qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant’s sponsor should be an active investigator in the area of the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sponsors are expected to be engaged researchers able to provide appropriate mentorship and oversight for the proposed training and research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training focus and environment
rubrics_metrics.description: In most cases, the postdoctoral fellowship supports research training experiences in new settings to maximize the acquisition of new skills and knowledge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applications are intended to enable fellows to gain new skills—often by moving to a different research environment—so proposals should justify how the proposed setting and training will expand the applicant’s capabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of training toward degree requirements for health professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: For those who have a health professional degree, the proposed training may be used to satisfy a portion of the degree requirements for a master’s degree, a doctoral degree, or other advanced research degree program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Health-professional applicants should indicate how the proposed F32 training fits with any concurrent degree requirements, if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awarded support components (duration and costs covered)
rubrics_metrics.description: Postdoctoral fellowship awards provide a stipend based on the level of experience, tuition and fees if specific courses are required, and an institutional allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards may cover up to three years of support; budget and stipend follow NRSA/NIEHS policies regarding level-based stipends, allowable tuition/fees, and institutional allowances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relevance to NIEHS mission / contacting program staff
rubrics_metrics.description: For information regarding the relevance of proposed projects to the mission interests of NIEHS, applicants may contact the NIEHS staff member listed on the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants are encouraged to contact the named program official to confirm alignment of their proposal with NIEHS priorities before submitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program announcement reference
rubrics_metrics.description: The latest Program Announcement for this fellowship is PA-21-048.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should consult PA-21-048 for full program details, instructions, and official policy language when preparing the application.
